title: Hadith Knowledge
description: General User → Beginner. Basic knowledge about hadith, familiar Prophetic teachings and short everyday applications. All questions are Beginner level; no hadith-number memorization or technical hadith terminology is required.
levelMethod: Beginner describes the knowledge required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Linked hadith texts and the source introduction were checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original educational paraphrases, not verbatim hadith translations. This is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: What does a Prophetic hadith report?

options.text: The Prophet's words, actions or approvals
Only the names of Quran chapters
Only events after the Prophet's lifetime
Only the opinions of modern writers

questions.explanation: Hadith preserve reports about Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), including his speech, conduct and approvals.

questions.question: Which is a well-known collection of hadith?
questions.explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari is a hadith collection; the other options are chapters of the Quran.

questions.question: Who heard the Prophet's teachings and passed them to others?

options.text: Only people who never met him

questions.explanation: The Companions heard and conveyed his teachings. In this report, he asked those present to inform those absent.

questions.question: According to a famous hadith, deeds are judged by what?
questions.explanation: Our purpose matters to Allah; two outwardly similar deeds can have different intentions.

questions.question: What does the Prophet teach about speech?

options.text: Speak what is good or remain silent
Say everything that comes to mind

questions.explanation: The hadith connects faith with responsible speech, care for neighbors and hospitality.

questions.question: Who is truly strong according to the Prophet?

options.text: Someone who never asks for help

questions.explanation: The hadith praises self-control when angry, rather than physical dominance.

questions.question: Which quality does the Prophet say leads to righteousness?
questions.explanation: Telling the truth leads toward righteous conduct and Paradise.

questions.question: Which good deeds are especially beloved to Allah?

options.text: Those done only when people watch
Those maintained regularly, even if small

questions.explanation: Consistency matters. A small good deed kept up regularly is valuable.

questions.question: Which activity does a famous hadith praise?
questions.explanation: The Prophet praised those who learn the Quran and teach it.

questions.question: Which hand did the Prophet teach a child to eat with?

options.text: The left hand as the usual choice
Different hands at random for each bite

questions.explanation: The teaching includes mentioning Allah, eating with the right hand and taking food from nearby.

questions.question: Who was named first when a man asked who deserved his best companionship?
questions.explanation: The Prophet emphasized the mother's right repeatedly, then mentioned the father.

questions.question: Whose rights did Jibril repeatedly emphasize to the Prophet?
questions.explanation: Jibril repeatedly urged good treatment of neighbors.

questions.question: What quality did the Prophet show when kissing his grandson?
questions.explanation: The report shows affection toward children and warns against being unmerciful.

questions.question: What can count as charity according to hadith?
questions.explanation: Charity includes helpful conduct and kind speech, as well as giving money.

questions.question: Which small act did the Prophet encourage?

options.text: Meeting someone with a cheerful face

questions.explanation: We should not dismiss small acts of goodness, including a warm expression.

questions.question: What does the Prophet say makes conduct more beautiful?
questions.explanation: Gentleness improves the way we deal with others.

questions.question: What is described in hadith as half of faith?
questions.explanation: The hadith highlights purification, alongside prayer, charity, patience and remembrance.

questions.question: Which pair of actions did the Prophet praise?
questions.explanation: The hadith praises feeding people and greeting both familiar and unfamiliar people.

questions.question: What did the Prophet encourage toward sick people?
questions.explanation: The Prophet encouraged visiting the sick and feeding the hungry.

questions.question: How serious is deliberately inventing a saying and attributing it to the Prophet?

options.text: It is allowed to gain followers

questions.explanation: The Prophet gave a severe warning against knowingly lying about him.

questions.question: Can a report of the Prophet's actions be a hadith?

options.text: Yes, hadith include actions as well as words
No, actions can never be reported

questions.explanation: Hadith are not limited to spoken statements; reports of conduct and approvals are included.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ask those present to do with his teaching?

options.text: Keep it only for their families
Sell it only to wealthy people

questions.explanation: The instruction helped his teaching reach people who were not there to hear it directly.

questions.question: Does a good intention make it acceptable to invent a hadith?

options.text: No, words must not be falsely attributed to the Prophet
Yes, if no author is named

questions.explanation: A worthy aim does not justify knowingly making up a Prophetic statement.

questions.question: What is an intention in the hadith about deeds?

options.text: The amount of time on a clock

questions.explanation: An intention is why someone chooses to act; sincerity is central to worship.

questions.question: What should a believer wish for a fellow Muslim?

options.text: The good they wish for themselves

questions.explanation: The hadith teaches sincere goodwill toward one's fellow believer.

questions.question: Which two sources of harm are specifically mentioned in a hadith about a Muslim?
questions.explanation: The report emphasizes protecting others from harmful words and actions.

questions.question: Which behavior is warned against as a trait of hypocrisy?
questions.explanation: The warning calls us to examine our conduct; it is not a license to label people over a single mistake.

questions.question: What quality did the Prophet praise among the best people?
questions.explanation: The Prophet linked excellence with good manners and character.

questions.question: Can a true but hurtful comment about an absent person still be backbiting?

options.text: Yes, truth alone does not make such speech acceptable
No, true comments can never be backbiting
Only if it is written in a book

questions.explanation: The hadith distinguishes backbiting from slander: a false allegation adds another wrong. Legitimate reporting of harm is a separate matter.

questions.question: What does Allah regard rather than appearance and wealth in this hadith?
questions.explanation: The teaching directs attention to the heart and conduct, rather than outward status.

questions.question: Is charity limited to giving money?

options.text: No, practical help can also be charity
Yes, only wealthy people can give it

questions.explanation: The report includes helping with transport, kind words and removing hazards among acts of charity.

questions.question: What does hadith say about removing something harmful from a path?

options.text: It is valuable only if paid
It is only a ruler's concern
It has no connection with goodness
It is an act of charity

questions.explanation: Making a shared path safer is one of the charitable actions named in the report.

questions.question: What does the story of giving water to a thirsty dog teach?

options.text: Kindness to animals can be rewarded

questions.explanation: The Prophet affirmed reward for caring for living creatures.

questions.question: What encouragement does hadith give someone seeking religious knowledge?

options.text: Allah eases a path to Paradise for the learner

questions.explanation: Seeking knowledge is a valuable path; beginners can start with reliable, accessible learning.

questions.question: What does hadith teach about helping a fellow Muslim?

options.text: Help is worthwhile only when public
Allah helps His servant who helps their brother

questions.explanation: The report encourages easing others' difficulties and offering support.

questions.question: In the hadith describing religion as sincere counsel, what attitude belongs toward fellow Muslims?
questions.explanation: Sincere counsel includes wishing people well and guiding them honestly.

questions.question: How did the Prophet tell people to teach and encourage others?

options.text: Make things easy and offer glad tidings

questions.explanation: The instruction promotes encouragement and avoids unnecessary difficulty.

questions.question: When choosing the easier of two options, what condition did the Prophet observe?

options.text: It must impress the most people
The option must not be sinful
It must be the least familiar

questions.explanation: Ease is valued within obedience to Allah; it does not make a sinful choice acceptable.

questions.question: What is prayer compared to in a well-known hadith?
questions.explanation: The report describes prayer as light and highlights several other forms of worship.

questions.question: What advice did the Prophet repeat to a man seeking counsel?

options.text: Do not give in to anger

questions.explanation: This brief counsel encourages guarding oneself against anger and its harmful consequences.

questions.question: A post labels an unfamiliar quote as a hadith without a source. What should you do before sharing it as the Prophet's words?

options.text: Check a reliable source or ask a qualified person
Forward it because it is popular
Add a hadith number of your own
Assume every religious quote is authentic

questions.explanation: Checking before attribution is a practical way to avoid spreading false statements about the Prophet.

questions.question: You are about to donate. Which intention best reflects the hadith about deeds?

options.text: Seeking Allah's pleasure and helping someone
Proving you are richer than everyone

questions.explanation: A donation should be guided by sincerity rather than a desire to show off.

questions.question: A group chat is becoming insulting. Which response follows the teaching about good speech?

options.text: Spread the insults to another group
Use helpful words or refrain from joining in
Invent a rumor to distract people

questions.explanation: Responsible speech includes refusing to add harmful words to a conversation.

questions.question: Someone insults you. What best reflects the strength praised in hadith?

options.text: Control your response without abusing them

questions.explanation: Choosing self-control in anger shows the strength described by the Prophet.

questions.question: You made an error at work. Which response follows the teaching on truthfulness?

options.text: Explain honestly and work to correct it
Alter the records to hide it

questions.explanation: Truthfulness remains important when admitting a mistake feels uncomfortable.

questions.question: Which voluntary learning plan best reflects the hadith about regular deeds?

options.text: A huge target you abandon immediately
A manageable amount you can continue daily
Studying only when someone praises you

questions.explanation: A realistic, steady habit applies the teaching about consistent good deeds.

questions.question: You can accurately help a beginner read a short surah. Which action follows the teaching about learning and teaching Quran?

options.text: Pretend to know what you do not
Teach patiently within what you know

questions.explanation: Passing on Quran knowledge carefully and patiently puts this teaching into practice.

questions.question: You sit down to a shared meal. Which practice matches the Prophet's guidance to a child?

options.text: Reach across everyone for each bite
Start by criticizing the other guests
Take food from someone else's plate
Mention Allah, use the right hand and eat from nearby

questions.explanation: The report gives simple table manners that can be practiced at everyday meals.

questions.question: Your mother asks for reasonable help while you are free. Which action reflects her right to good companionship?

options.text: Insist she should never ask you

questions.explanation: The hadith emphasizes a mother's right to care and good companionship.

questions.question: An elderly neighbor is struggling with groceries. Which response reflects care for neighbors?
questions.explanation: Offering considerate help is a practical expression of the neighborly care emphasized in hadith.

questions.question: A young child is upset. Which approach reflects the Prophet's mercy toward children?
questions.explanation: Mercy and appropriate affection belong in our treatment of children.

questions.question: You have no money to donate today. What charitable act can you still offer?
questions.explanation: A good word is one of the nonfinancial forms of charity mentioned in hadith.

questions.question: You meet a classmate who seems left out. Which simple act fits the teaching about small good deeds?

options.text: Turn their loneliness into a joke

questions.explanation: A friendly welcome applies the encouragement not to dismiss small acts of goodness.

questions.question: A beginner asks the same question again. Which response reflects gentleness?
questions.explanation: Gentleness improves how we teach and interact with others.

questions.question: A friend leaves a book with you for safekeeping. Which action avoids betraying that trust?

options.text: Hide it and deny receiving it
Protect it and return it as agreed
Give it away as though it were yours

questions.explanation: Safeguarding what someone entrusts to us is the opposite of betrayal.

questions.question: You notice a small obstacle on a walkway and can safely move it. What should you do?

options.text: Push it where people are more likely to trip
Hide it under a loose mat
Remove it so people can pass safely

questions.explanation: Removing a hazard applies the charitable action described in the hadith.

questions.question: A thirsty animal can safely be given water. Which action reflects the lesson of the hadith?

options.text: Tease it with an empty bowl

questions.explanation: The report encourages compassionate care for animals.

questions.question: Friends are mocking an absent person's faults for entertainment. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid joining in and redirect the talk
Record the mockery to spread it
Say it is always fine if true

questions.explanation: Being true does not automatically make such talk acceptable; the hadith warns against backbiting.

questions.question: A friend is ill and welcomes a visit. Which action follows the Prophet's encouragement?

options.text: Insist their illness makes them worthless

questions.explanation: A considerate visit is one way to care for someone who is unwell.

questions.question: Someone has just begun learning Islam. Which approach follows the instruction to encourage and ease learning?

options.text: Overwhelm them to prove your knowledge
Explain a simple next step and encourage them

questions.explanation: Clear, encouraging teaching helps a new learner progress without unnecessary hardship.
